correctness.rationale: For odd n and p=char(F_q) not dividing n, Fourier inversion is valid and the product e_x e_y=e_{2y−x} gives c_k=c_{−k}c_{2k}. The nonzero support is invariant under both finite permutations. Multiplication of equations at k and −k, then cancellation and surjectivity of doubling on the support, give c_{−k}c_k=1 and c_{2k}=c_k². On order-r indices, if −1=2^{d_r/2} modulo r the seed relation t^{2^{d_r/2}}=t^{−1} also closes the doubling cycle; otherwise the negated doubling cycle is disjoint and independently given by inversion, with closure t^{2^{d_r}−1}=1. Frobenius covariance c_{qk}=c_k^q is both necessary and sufficient by inversion. The quotient of the order-r residues by H_r has q-cycles of common length s_r. On each cycle, propagation gives one zero choice or a seed solving both t^{N_r}=1 and t^{q^{s_r}−ε_r2^{a_r}}=1. The gcd is prime to p: N_r is odd if p=2, and the second exponent is a unit modulo p if p is odd. Thus the number of nonzero choices is the stated gcd, even when the exponent difference vanishes in characteristic two. Independent cycles and c_0=0 or 1 give the formula and inverse. Direct exact enumeration in the original basis independently gave 12, 16 and 80 at (n,q)=(5,4),(7,3),(9,2).
residual_risks: The bounded counts do not prove the universal formula. Even n and the modular case p|n are outside the finding.

evidence: Put S=ord_n(q), m=S/s_r and e=ε_r2^{a_r}. The map H_r→(Z/N_r Z)^× sending the generators 2 and −1 to 2 and −1 is well defined: 2^{d_r}=1 mod N_r and, when the generators are dependent, 2^{d_r/2}=−1 mod N_r. In the other branch the group is the direct product of the doubling subgroup and ⟨−1⟩.

Hence e^m≡1 mod N_r because (q^{s_r} mod r)^m=1. If g=gcd(N_r,q^{s_r}−e), then q^S≡e^m≡1 mod g. Therefore gcd(N_r,q^S−1,|q^{s_r}−e|)=g, including a vanishing difference. Equivalently, a propagated seed closes automatically in the splitting field.

On the exact order-r stratum, write k=(n/r)u with u a unit modulo r. Its ⟨−1,2,q⟩-orbit consists of a full q-cycle on cosets of H_r. The old orbit parameters d,t,a,M_D become r,d_r,s_r,N_r, respectively. There are φ(r)/(h_rs_r) such cycles.
In the branch −1∈⟨2⟩, choose the older ε=1 and b=a_r; otherwise the sign and power are unique and equal to the frozen choices. Thus the closing exponent q^{s_r}−ε_r2^{a_r} is the same.

value.rationale: The arithmetic classification is a worthwhile invariant of a natural algebra. But the incremental assertion in this submission is the same known classification in divisor notation: the exponent just counts same-order cycles and the gcd simplification follows immediately from closure. Neither supplies a further mathematical invariant or substantive new range, obstruction, application or algorithmic result. There is no isolated surviving valuable claim to repair.
residual_risks: Convenience of presentation is distinct from a new scientific finding; no claim is made about the usefulness or attribution of the prior census itself.
